He played [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington Colonials]] (now Revolutionaries), becoming the first Japanese-born [[student athlete]] to secure an [[NCAA Division I]] basketball [[athletic scholarship|scholarship]].[https://www.nytimes.com/2015/01/21/sports/george-washingtons-yuta-watanabe-hopes-to-inspire-players-in-japan.html "Coming off the bench, a basketball ambassador"], ''[[New York Times]]'' He was named [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] Defensive Player of the Year in 2018. He has also represented the [[Japan national basketball team|Japan national team]], helping them win the bronze medal at the [[East Asia Basketball Championship|2013 East Asia Basketball Championship]]. Before moving to the collegiate level, Watanabe attended Jinsei Gakuen High School in [[Zentsūji, Kagawa]]. He later transferred to St. Thomas More Preparatory School in [[Oakdale, Connecticut]] in 2013. Watanabe rose to fame in his high school program, and was one of their most valuable players in the National Prep School Invitational as a senior in 2014. In college, he became the fourth-ever Japanese-born Division I basketball player. ==High school career== Watanabe attended Jinsei Gakuen High School in Kagawa. He led the basketball team to the runner-up spot of the All-Japan High School Basketball Tournament in his final two years with the program. While in Jinsei Gakuen, Watanabe said his career goal was to make it to the NCAA and ultimately join the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].{{cite web |last1=Nagatsuka |first1=Kaz |date=13 May 2013 |title=Japan's 'chosen one' has big dreams |url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2013/05/13/basketball/japans-chosen-one-has-big-dreams/ |access-date=6 September 2014 |website=JapanTimes.co.jp}}{{cite web|last1=Nagatsuka|first1=Kaz|title=Teen standout Watanabe faces major challenges in pursuit of NBA dream|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2013/06/09/basketball/teen-standout-watanabe-faces-major-challenges-in-pursuit-of-nba-dream/|website=[[The Japan Times]]|date=9 June 2013 |access-date=6 September 2014}} In late 2013, Watanabe traveled to the United States and attended [[St. Thomas More School (Connecticut)|St. Thomas More Preparatory School]] in [[Oakdale, Connecticut]]. At the conclusion of his sole high school season outside his native country, Watanabe averaged 13 points and six rebounds. He helped the team reach a 26–8 overall record and a ticket to the National Prep Championship game. On January 31, 2014, in his first appearance in the annual National Prep School Invitational, Watanabe scored 12 points versus [[Suffield Academy]]. He contributed 20 points and six rebounds in a 70–61 victory against Canarias Basketball Academy from Spain.{{cite web|title=17th Annual National Prep School Invitational|url=http://netscoutsbasketball.com/camps/national-prep-school-invitational/|website=NetScoutsBasketball.com|date=21 January 2013 |access-date=22 January 2015}} As a result, he was named to the National Prep School Invitational All-Tournament Team and garnered prestigious [[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]] (NEPSAC) Class AAA First Team All-League honors.{{cite web|title=Yuta Watanabe Bio|url=http://www.gwsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/yuta_watanabe_898135.html|access-date=30 July 2014|website=GWSports.com|archive-date=3 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403033248/http://www.gwsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/yuta_watanabe_898135.html|url-status=dead}} Watanabe was also labeled "the Chosen One" by ''[[The Japan Times]]''. Watanabe was rated a 77 (three-star recruit) by [[ESPN]] Recruiting Nation. He was also given a three-star rating by [[Scout.com]] and the same composite grade. ==College career== {{multiple image | align = right | direction = horizontal | width = | image1 = Matsui keijuro (cropped).jpg | width1 = 122 | alt1 = | image2 = Takahashi michael (cropped).jpg | width2 = 114 | alt2 = | image3 = Taishi Ito.JPG | width3 = 95 | alt3 = | header = | header_align = | header_background = | footer = Watanabe was the fourth Japan-born basketball player to compete in NCAA Division I, the first three being [[KJ Matsui]] (left), [[Michael Takahashi]] (center), and Taishi Ito (right) | footer_align = | footer_background = | background color = }} In fall 2014, [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington Colonials]] head coach [[Mike Lonergan]] received a phone call from Jamie Cosgrove, a coach at [[Trinity College (Connecticut)|Trinity College]] who saw Watanabe play with St. Thomas More.{{cite news|last1=Feinstein|first1=John|title=Yuta Watanabe, Japan's 'Chosen One,' hopes his path to GW leads to NBA|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/yuta-watanabe-japans-chosen-one-hopes-his-path-to-gw-leads-to-nba/2015/01/14/f3ecfe4e-9bff-11e4-a7ee-526210d665b4_story.html|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=16 January 2015}} Watanabe eventually committed to play for GWU. This allowed him to attend GWU in the 2014-15 year as a freshman.{{cite web|title=Yuta Watanabe|url=http://www.verbalcommits.com/players/yuta-watanabe|website=VerbalCommits.com|access-date=6 September 2014|archive-date=24 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221124113254/https://www.verbalcommits.com/players/yuta-watanabe|url-status=dead}} It was made official when Watanabe posted the message through [[Twitter]], "I've decided to go to George Washington University. The school has a good basketball team, too. I'm sure I'll have hard times both in basketball and academics, but I'll give it my best shot."{{cite web|last1=Nagatsuka|first1=Kaz|title=Watanabe opts to go to George Washington U.|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2014/02/05/basketball/watanabe-opts-to-go-to-george-washington-u/|website=[[The Japan Times]]|date=5 February 2014 |access-date=6 September 2014}} According to ESPN, his second option was [[Fordham Rams men's basketball|Fordham]], who gave Watanabe an offer to join their team as well. He became the first Japanese-born male player to get an [[Division I (NCAA)|NCAA Division I]] basketball [[athletic scholarship|scholarship]]{{cite news|last=Berkman|first=Seth|title=Coming Off the Bench, a Basketball Ambassador|date=January 20, 2015|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/01/21/sports/george-washingtons-yuta-watanabe-hopes-to-inspire-players-in-japan.html?ref=sports&_r=0|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201143926/https://www.nytimes.com/2015/01/21/sports/george-washingtons-yuta-watanabe-hopes-to-inspire-players-in-japan.html?ref=sports&_r=0|archive-date=December basketball at that level.{{#tag:ref|The other three were [[KJ Matsui]] ([[Columbia Lions men's basketball|Columbia]]), Taishi Ito ([[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland]]) and [[Michael Takahashi]] ([[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge]]).{{cite web|title=12 Yuta House|url=https://gwtoday.gwu.edu/gw-basketball-holds-court-white-house|access-date=2021-04-20|website=gwtoday.gwu.edu}} Regarding Watanabe's collegiate career, former Japanese college basketball player [[KJ Matsui]] said, "It's good for Nabe-chan (Watanabe) to play at a competitive team, but he's going to have to battle for playing time."{{cite web|last1=Nagatsuka|first1=Kaz|title=Encouragement, advice helped steer Watanabe to GWU|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2014/02/19/basketball/encouragement-advice-helped-steer-watanabe-to-gwu/|website=[[The Japan Times]]|date=19 February 2014 |access-date=14 September 2014}} The Colonials had four other recruits coming into the program for [[2014–15 George Washington Colonials men's basketball team|2014–15]]: Anthony Swan, Darian Bryant, Matt Cimino, and Paul Jorgensen.{{cite web|title=2014 Geo. Washington Basketball Commitment List|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/commitments/2014/georgewashington-632|website=[[Yahoo!]]|access-date=23 January 2015}} After he joined [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]] in 2014, featured profiles of Watanabe were published by major American newspapers such as ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[The Washington Post]]''.{{cite web|title=Washington Post, New York Times Profile GW's Yuta Watanabe|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=31600&ATCLID=209859325|website=Atlantic10.com| date=21 January 2015 |access-date=22 January 2015}} On Watanabe's athletic caliber and exceptional career breakthrough into the NBA, where players of East Asian descent are uncommon, former [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball]] player and half-Chinese [[Zach Chu]] said, "To see someone of Asian descent, and play as well as he does, it's cool for college basketball, really cool for the Asian community." The George Washington athletics website received the second-most views from Japan in hits by country, ranked behind only the U.S. On many occasions, he was congratulated on the school's campus. Speaking on his ethnic and racial background, sporting fame and athletic legacy, he said, "Japanese are thinking Americans are bigger and taller and more athletic. They are thinking it's more difficult for Japanese to play in NCAA, but I'm playing right now, so I want to make other people come to the United States." NBA-bound players of East Asian ancestry such as Matsui, [[Yao Ming]], [[Jeremy Lin]], and [[Yuki Togashi]] have been the target of racist comments in the past, but Watanabe apparently did not receive racially insensitive remarks in his first few years in the NBA and the U.S. Nevertheless, he said, "If they said something racist, I don't care." === Freshman === [[File:Yuta Watanabe GW.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Watanabe playing for George Washington in February 2015]] On November 14, 2014, Watanabe made his debut for [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]], against [[Grambling State Tigers men's basketball|Grambling State]], finishing with eight points, seven rebounds and a block in 20 minutes, contributing to the team's 92–40 win, its largest win since 1999.{{cite web|title=Garino, George Washington beat Grambling St. 92-40|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400591080|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=24 December 2014}}{{cite web|title=Grambling St Tigers vs. George Washington Colonials Box Score|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400591080|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=24 December 2014}} On December 12, Watanabe was named [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] Rookie of the Week after averaging 9.0 points and 4.7 rebounds in three games as he helped the team win the 2014 [[Diamond Head Classic]] crown.{{Cite web|title=GW's Larsen, Watanabe Sweep Atlantic 10 Hoops Weekly Awards|url=https://gwsports.com/news/2014/12/29/gw_s_larsen_watanabe_sweep_atlantic_10_hoops_weekly_awards.aspx|access-date=2021-04-20|website=George Washington University Athletics|language=en}} Watanabe hit a key three-pointer with 3 minutes and 32 seconds remaining to upset [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] with a 60–54 win on December 25.{{cite web|title=George Washington upsets No. 11 Wichita State in final of Diamond Head Classic|url=http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2014/dec/25/george-washington-upsets-no-11-wichita-st-60-54/?page=all|website=[[The Washington Times]]|access-date=22 January 2015}} On March 7, he set a career-high 21 points, knocking down seven 3-pointers, against [[UMass Minutemen basketball|Massachusetts]].{{cite web|title=Yuta Watanabe Game Log 2014-15 Regular Season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3133838/type/mens-college-basketball/year/2015|access-date=16 January 2015|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} On March 9, Watanabe earned his second Atlantic 10 Rookie of the Week honor, becoming the first to earn multiple Rookie of the Week awards in the same season since [[Lasan Kromah]] earned three in 2009–10. He led the Colonials to a 2–0 final week of the Atlantic 10 regular season with a team-best 13.5 points on 53 percent shooting, including 64 percent behind the arc, along with five rebounds and two assists.{{Cite web|title=Kalinoksi, Watanabe Earn Final Weekly Awards|url=http://atlantic10.com/news/2015/3/9/209936019.aspx|access-date=2021-04-20|website=atlantic10.com|date=9 March 2015 }}{{Cite web|title=GW Men's Hoops' Watanabe Earns Second A-10 Rookie of the Week Award|url=https://gwsports.com/news/2015/3/9/GW_Men_s_Hoops_Watanabe_Earns_Second_A_10_Rookie_of_the_Week_Award.aspx|access-date=2021-04-20|website=George Washington University Athletics|language=en}} As a freshman, Watanabe was a key bench player and an instrumental element on the Colonials' rotation. He was often awarded playing time in late-game situations. Head coach [[Mike Lonergan]] said, "With Yuta, we have scoring off the bench. If I start Yuta, we have no scoring off the bench at all." === Sophomore === On March 5, 2016, Watanabe posted career-highs in scoring and assists with 22 points and six assists in George Washington's 87–80 loss to [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]].{{Cite web|title=Yuta Watanabe Game Log 2015-16 Regular Season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3133838/type/mens-college-basketball/year/2016|access-date=2021-04-20|website=[[ESPN]]}} On March 31, he logged a team-high 19 points and a career-high four blocks as George Washington won the [[2016 National Invitation Tournament]] with a 76–60 win over [[Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball|Valparaiso]].{{Cite web|title=GW Men's Basketball Wins NIT Championship|url=https://gwsports.com/news/2016/3/31/GW_Men_s_Basketball_Wins_NIT_Championship.aspx|access-date=2021-04-21|website=GWSports.com}} It was the first time in program history the team won a postseason championship. Overall, Watanabe was the team's leader in blocked shots with 40, ranking second in the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]]. His 8.4 points per game was the fifth best on the team. === Junior === On November 15, 2016, Watanabe logged his first double-double with 13 points and 12 rebounds in a 77–75 victory over [[Siena Saints men's basketball|Siena]]. On January 8, 2017, he had a career-high three steals in a game against [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]]. Watanabe scored a season-high 21 points in an 80–71 loss against [[UIC Flames men's basketball|Illinois]] on March 20.{{Cite web|title=Yuta Watanabe Game Log 2016-17 Regular Season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3133838/type/mens-college-basketball/year/2017|access-date=2021-04-20|website=[[ESPN]]}} As a junior, Watanabe was the second-leading scorer at George Washington at 12.2 points per game.{{Cite web|title=Yuta Watanabe Biography|url=https://gwsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/yuta-watanabe/6153|access-date=2021-04-21|website=GWSports.com}} He was also named to the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] All-Defensive Team.{{Cite web|title=Cline Named Atlantic 10 Player of the Year, Miller Voted as Coach of the Year|url=http://atlantic10.com/news/2017/3/7/211515812.aspx|access-date=2021-04-20|website=atlantic10.com|date=7 March 2017 }} === Senior === On November 20, 2017, Watanabe grabbed a career-high 13 rebounds versus [[Rider Broncs men's basketball|Rider]].{{Cite web|title=Yuta Watanabe Game Log 2017-18 Regular Season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3133838/type/mens-college-basketball/year/2018|access-date=2021-04-20|website=ESPN|language=en}} On November 29, he logged a career-high five steals against [[Morgan State Bears men's basketball|Morgan State]]. In his final game for the Colonials on February 28, 2018, Watanabe scored a career-high 31 points in a 72–56 win over [[Fordham Rams men's basketball|Fordham]] .{{Cite web|date=2018-03-01|title=Watanabe says an emotional goodbye to the Smith Center|url=https://www.gwhatchet.com/2018/03/01/watanabe-says-an-emotional-goodbye-to-the-smith-center/|access-date=2021-04-26|website=The GW Hatchet}} As a senior, Watanabe was George Washington's leading scorer at 16.3 points per game and second-leading rebounder with 6.1 per game, while also leading the team in blocks with 54. He was named the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] Defensive Player of the Year,{{cite news|last=Buckner|first=Candace|title=In Japan, he is 'The Chosen One.' Can Yuta Watanabe become the country's second-ever NBA player?|date=July 12, 2018|newspaper=The Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/in-japan-he-is-the-chosen-one-can-yuta-watanabe-become-the-countrys-second-ever-nba-player/2018/07/12/ba3fab50-853b-11e8-9e80-403a221946a7_story.html}}{{Cite web|title=Aldridge, Adams Named Atlantic 10 Co-Players of the Year, Rhode Island's Hurley Voted as Coach of the Year|url=http://atlantic10.com/news/2018/3/6/211704410.aspx|access-date=2021-04-20|website=atlantic10.com|date=6 March 2018 }} becoming the first Colonial to win the award.{{cite news|last=Odeven|first=Ed|title=Yuta Watanabe reflects on successful hoop career at George Washington|date=April 13, 2018|newspaper=The Japan Times|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2018/04/13/basketball/yuta-watanabe-reflects-successful-hoop-career-george-washington/}} Watanabe also made the Atlantic 10 All-Conference's Third Team and Atlantic 10 All-Defensive Team. He also received George Washington's [[Patricio Garino]] Defensive Award and [[Mike Brown (basketball, born 1963)|Mike Brown]] MVP Award, both awards named after the former basketball alumni.{{Cite web|title=Men's Basketball Hands Out Awards at Team Banquet|url=https://gwsports.com/news/2018/3/5/Men_s_Basketball_Hands_Out_Awards_at_Team_Banquet.aspx|access-date=2021-04-20|website=George Washington University Athletics|language=en}} At the conclusion of Watanabe's college career, he ranked near the top of key categories in GWU history including second in blocked shots (147), second in games played (134) and 15th in scoring (1,460). ==Professional career== ===Memphis Grizzlies (2018–2020)=== [[File:Rui Hachimura Yuta Watanabe (50640688868).jpg|thumb|right|Watanabe (right) and [[Rui Hachimura]] in 2020]] [[File:Yuta Watanabe (50641445461).jpg|thumb|upright|right|Watanabe with the Grizzlies in 2020]] After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Watanabe played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the [[2018 NBA Summer League]]. Afterwards, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{Cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Yuta Watanabe to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-yuta-watanabe-to-two-way-contract-180720|access-date=2021-03-30|website=Memphis Grizzlies|language=en}} On October 27, 2018, Watanabe made his NBA debut, coming off the bench with two points and two rebounds in a 117–96 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He became the second Japanese player to play in the NBA after [[Yuta Tabuse]], who debuted with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in 2004.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070761|title=Gasol, Conley lead Grizzlies to easy win over Suns 117-96|work=ESPN.com|date=October 27, 2018|access-date=October 27, 2018}} Though he spent the majority of the season in the G League with the Hustle, the Grizzlies were third behind the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[Golden State Warriors]] in merchandise sold in Japan due to Watanabe's presence.{{cite news |last1=Buckner |first1=Candace |title=For Wizards' Rui Hachimura, Memphis trip brings a pair of special reunions |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/12/15/wizards-rui-hachimura-memphis-trip-brings-pair-special-reunions/ |access-date=January 6, 2020 |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |date=December 15, 2019}} In the G League, Watanabe started in 32 of 33 games, averaging 14.2 points, 7.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.1 blocks in 33.9 minutes while shooting 43.6 percent from the field and 33.1 percent from 3-point range.{{Cite web|title=Yuta Watanabe G-League Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/w/watanyu01d.html|access-date=2021-04-20|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}{{Cite web|last=Odeven|first=Ed|date=2019-04-18|title=Yuta Watanabe makes positive impact as a rookie|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2019/04/18/basketball/yuta-watanabe-makes-positive-impact-rookie/|access-date=2021-04-20|website=The Japan Times|language=en-US}} Watanabe shared his time playing back and forth for the Grizzlies and the Hustle for the season. On December 14, 2019, Watanabe and [[Rui Hachimura]] of the [[Washington Wizards]] became the first pair of Japanese players to share the court in the NBA.{{Cite web|last=|first=|title=Basketball: Hachimura, Watanabe meet on NBA court in first for Japan|url=https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2019/12/002bafda9fbb-basketball-hachimura-watanabe-meet-on-nba-court-in-first-for-japan.html|access-date=2021-04-04|website=Kyodo News+|date=15 December Other|url=https://nextshark.com/yuta-watanabe-rui-hachimura/|access-date=2021-04-04|website=NextShark|language=}} On January 4, 2020, Watanabe had a team-high 28 points on 12-of-19 field goal shooting and 2-of-4 from three, to go with seven rebounds, four blocks, two assists and two steals in the Hustle's 130–127 win over the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite news |title=Grizzlies' Yuta Watanabe: Posts big line in G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-yuta-watanabe-posts-big-line-in-g-league/ |access-date=January 6, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 5, 2020}} He scored a career-high 40 points on 14-of-20 shooting from the field and 8-of-11 from three on January 22, in a win versus the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite news |last1=Greer |first1=Jarvis |title=Hustle wins again as Yuta goes for 40 |url=https://www.wmcactionnews5.com/2020/01/23/hustle-wins-again-yuta-goes/ |access-date=January 23, 2020 |work=WMC Action News |date=January 22, 2020}}{{Cite web|last=Odeven|first=Ed|date=2020-01-23|title=Yuta Watanabe scores career-high 40 points in NBA G League game|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2020/01/23/basketball/yuta-watanabe-scores-career-high-40-points-nba-g-league-game/|access-date=2021-04-20|website=The Japan Times|language=en-US}} He led the Japanese squad in points and efficiency per game.{{Cite web |title=Japan at the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2019 |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/team/Japan |access-date=2021-05-02 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} ==Player profile== A spark-off-the-bench player,{{Cite web |date=2021-04-19 |title=Raptors Announce Signing of Japanese Forward Yuta Watanabe |url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/raptors-announce-signing-of-japanese-forward-yuta-watanabe/ |access-date=2021-04-21 |website=SLAM |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2021 |title=Raptors' sparkplug hopes for a basketball boom in Japan |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sparkplug-hopes-basketball-boom-japan |access-date=2021-04-21 |website=Toronto Raptors |language=en}} Watanabe is known for his defensive ability. As described by sports website [[theScore]], Watanabe "has great hands on the defensive end."{{Cite news |last=Casciaro |first=Joseph |date=4 February 2021 |title=The All-Nobody Team: 5 NBA players quickly becoming somebodies |url=https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/2106308 |access-date=2021-04-21 |website=theScore.com}} In 2019, [[SB Nation]] sportswriter Brandon Abraham lauded his defense, saying, "The Grizzlies and Hustle were simply better with Yuta on the court." [[Memphis Grizzlies]] TV [[play-by-play announcer]] Pete Pranica described his "defensive instinct" as "impressive." [[Toronto Raptors]] head coach [[Nick Nurse]] commented on his defense as well, saying that it "rub off on others." Watanabe earned praises for his basketball IQ, with theScore commenting, "He always seems to be in the right spot on both ends of the court." Pranica stated that Watanabe's IQ is one of his "greatest assets." [[Memphis Hustle]] assistant coach Antoine Broxsie was also impressed by his IQ. Watanabe's play has been described as "mistake-free." Nurse said in multiple interviews that Watanabe "doesn’t make mistakes" during games.{{Cite magazine |last=Rose |first=Aaron |title=Yuta Watanabe Is Proud of How Well He's Playing Lately |language=en |magazine=Sports Illustrated |url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/news/toronto-raptors-yuta-watanabe-getting-a-shot |access-date=2021-04-21}} Pranica also remarked that Watanabe "rarely made the same mistake twice after having been coached on it." His energy and hustle has also become his defining trait in the NBA,{{Cite web |last=Kern |first=Josh |date=2021-02-04 |title=What is Yuta Watanabe's role on this Raptors team? |url=https://www.raptorshq.com/2021/2/4/22262141/toronto-raptors-yuta-watanabe-role-block-nikola-vucevic |access-date=2021-04-21 |website=Raptors HQ |language=en}} impressing Nurse and fans. In addition, Watanabe has been praised for being constantly in motion,{{Cite web |last=Kern |first=Josh |date=2021-04-19 |title=Report: Raptors sign Watanabe to standard NBA deal |url=https://www.raptorshq.com/2021/4/19/22391548/report-toronto-raptors-sign-yuta-watanabe-standard-nba-deal |access-date=2021-04-21 |website=Raptors HQ |language=en}} which helped him to "always be a step ahead of the opposing offence" as noted by Raptors HQ of SB Nation. [[Sports Illustrated]] observed that Watanabe "plays like his feet are on fire," and that he is "constantly running around, jumping in and out of attacking lanes, and wreaking havoc on opposing offences." Nurse also stated that his constant motion helps the team's offence. Watanabe has been criticized because of his lack of weight and muscle from his college career even until he turned professional. [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]] head coach [[Mike Lonergan]] said that he hoped that he weighed over 200 pounds by the start of his sophomore season. [[KJ Matsui]] commented on his frame as well, saying, "If he puts more muscles and get big, he will be unstoppable." Pranica also pointed out that Watanabe "needs to get physically bigger and stronger so that he is not overmatched." [[File:Yuta Watanabe Japan.jpg|thumb|right|270px|Watanabe against [[Hong Kong national basketball team|Hong Kong]] in 2013]] Watanabe supposedly lacked panache at the time he joined the George Washington basketball program, with teammate [[Kevin Larsen (basketball)|Kevin Larsen]] commenting, "We told him to find a new celebration because the one he had wasn't cutting it. He was, like, jumping in the air making a weird face. So we tried to help him find a new one." Watanabe sometimes mimicks [[Carmelo Anthony]], using the "three to the dome" celebration after making three-pointers. ==Personal life== Watanabe was born on October 13, 1994, in [[Yokohama, Kanagawa]], in Japan, and grew up in [[Miki, Kagawa]].{{Cite web |last=Reiland |first=Mikeie |date=2019-09-05 |title=Japanese basketball's 'Chosen One' is playing in the G League |url=https://www.sbnation.com/2019/9/5/20849363/yuta-watanabe-rui-hachimura-japanese-basketball-future |access-date=2021-03-08 |website=SBNation.com |language=en}} Watanabe's family has a rich history in basketball. His mother, Kumi, played for the [[Chanson V-Magic]] and the [[Japan women's national basketball team|Japan women's national team]]. His father played for the [[Kumagai Gumi Bruins]] at the professional level. Watanabe's sister, Yuki, played with the [[Aisin AW Wings]]. During his childhood, Watanabe's favorite NBA team was the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and his favorite athlete was [[Kobe Bryant]].
